carriedFindings.claim: the banner this diff adds states "Each affected statement below is marked in place", and nine statements that requirements 37, 38, 42 and 44 overrule are left unmarked and now assert the opposite of what ships — including the endpoint's own query vocabulary, its response body and the sidebar's visibility rule

witness.detail: Unmarked and now false, each verified against HEAD: :35 "`user` and `viewer` have no access to this page" and :42 the matrix row "View Requests page | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌" — contradicted by requirement 37 and by apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts:325, which asserts 200 for both. :53 "**Default filter:** pending requests. The status filter can be changed to show approved, rejected, cancelled, or all statuses" and :142 "`status` — `pending` (default), `approved`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `all`" — the exact vocabulary the banner four lines above declares retired; `?status=pending` now answers 400 (apps/api/test/requests.spec.ts:1288). :214 "Status filter dropdown (`requests-status-filter`): options are "Pending" (default), "Approved", "Rejected", "Cancelled", "All"" — the shipped control renders All statuses/Open/Answered/Granted/Declined/Cancelled (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx:35), and e2e/tests/requests-page.spec.ts:146 now selects "Open", an option this line does not list. :61 and :208 "a **badge** with the count of pending requests" — contradicted by requirement 44 and by apps/web/src/layout/requests-badge-context.tsx:58, which sums waitingOnMe and vacation.pendingCount. :178 the `200` body's top-level `"pendingCount": 2, "totalCount": 15` — the envelope is now {requests, vacation:{requests,pendingCount}, counts:{waitingOnMe,total}} and `totalCount` is gone from the codebase entirely. :198 the Error Messages row "Requests page — forbidden | You do not have permission to view requests" — REQUESTS_PAGE_MESSAGES.viewForbidden (packages/validation/src/index.ts:1983) is now emitted by no route. :207 "Visible to `admin` and `manager` only. Not visible to `user` or `viewer`" — contradicted by requirement 38 and by apps/web/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx:83, which pushes the row unconditionally.

carriedFindings.suggestedFix: Mark each of the nine statements in place, in the style already used at :63, :67, :132 and :188. Routed to `code` and not `spec` because requirements 37, 38, 42 and 44 authorize every one of these amendments in writing — no human ruling is needed, only the bookkeeping handoff task T9 assigned to `specs/user-management/10-*.md`.

carriedFindings.claim: TC-10-INT-01 was amended by half: its Steps were moved onto the new `?status=open` vocabulary with an explicit note, and its Expected Result was left describing the retired top-level envelope, so the spec and the test that carries its id now assert different response shapes

witness.detail: TC-10-INT-01. specs/user-management/10-organization-requests-page.md:281 was amended to `GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests?status=open` with the note "(**Amended by requests/01 requirement 42:** was `?status=pending`…)", but :285 still reads "HTTP 200. Returns 3 requests across M1 and M2, each with member info, balance, and dates. `pendingCount: 3`". The test labelled `// TC-10-INT-01` at apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts:210 asserts the opposite shape: :232 `expect(res.body.vacation.requests).toHaveLength(3)`, :233 `expect(res.body.vacation.pendingCount).toBe(3)` and :236 `expect(res.body.requests).toEqual([])`. carriedFindings.suggestedFix: Amend the Expected Result alongside the Steps: "HTTP 200. `requests: []` — no `Request` rows exist in this fixture. `vacation.requests` holds 3 rows across M1 and M2, each with member info, balance and dates, and `vacation.pendingCount` is 3." Same routing as F1: requirement 42 already authorizes the amendment in writing.

notes.claim: the area README promises a reassignment filter that spec 01 requirement 36 says does not exist and that requirement 42's closed filter sets could not express

witness.detail: specs/requests/README.md:84 — 'Member soft-deleted | user-management/04 | Requests they raised or hold are retained and readable; open requests **addressed to** them are flagged `assigneeInactive` and surface in the reassignment filter | 01'. Against specs/requests/01-requests.md requirement 36 — 'There is no reassignment **filter**: requirement 42 enumerates the filters exhaustively and this is not one of them, so a request needing reassignment is found by its banner and not by narrowing the list.' Requirement 42's filters are type (all|access|question|vacation), status (all|open|answered|granted|declined|cancelled), projectId and q, and an unknown value in either closed set is a 400 rather than a fallback (apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:170-176), so a caller could not send the filter the README promises even if one were built. The README is the stale side: specs/requests/02-client-participants.md:160 defers to 'spec 01 requirement 36' for this exact behaviour.

notes.suggestedFix: replace 'and surface in the reassignment filter' with 'and draw the reassign banner and control on the row and the detail screen' — the behaviour requirement 36 and edge case 11 actually specify. Raised as a note, not a blocker: requirement 36 settles it in writing, so nothing in the plan is undecidable, but a human should correct the README before the next spec in this area is written against it.

notes.claim: the README says spec 01 adds 30 new keys to REQUEST_MESSAGES; the spec's own Error Messages table lists 31 and 31 are present in the code

The cited line 1746 is REQUEST_MESSAGES' position at the base commit f06c7d8; it is 1771 at HEAD because this branch's own additions moved it.

notes.suggestedFix: say 31, and drop the line number in favour of the symbol name — a count and a line in a document that no test reads will drift again. No behaviour depends on either, which is why this is a note.

notes.claim: the 400 body for an unknown scope/status/type carries the literal 'unknown_value' in the same `fields` map that elsewhere holds REQUEST_MESSAGES copy, and the spec fixes neither the shape nor the answer for an unknown scope

witness.detail: GET .../requests?status=pending returns {error:'validation_error', fields:{status:'unknown_value'}}, pinned by apps/api/test/requests.spec.ts:1288 and apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts:431-435. Everywhere else in this spec a `fields` entry holds user-facing copy (e.g. fields.title = 'Enter a title'). Recorded as an accepted risk in the handoff. The spec is silent, so it is a note; a person should decide it in the spec rather than in a test.

notes.suggestedFix: State the 400 body for an unknown status/type/scope in the GET contract, or emit a REQUEST_MESSAGES string so no path can put 'unknown_value' in front of a person.

notes.claim: assigneeInvalid is returned under fields.assigneeMembershipId while Validation Rules row 7 names the field assigneeKind, so a client could look under the wrong key

notes.claim: waitingOnMe hardcodes status: { in: ['open','answered'] } rather than deriving the non-terminal set from TERMINAL_REQUEST_STATUSES, so a sixth non-terminal status added later would silently vanish from the badge that is this feature's only notification channel

witness.detail: isTerminalRequestStatus / TERMINAL_REQUEST_STATUSES already exist at packages/validation/src/requests.ts:58-66 and are used by every other non-terminal test in the service (:423, :493, :600, :713). Requirement 47 makes the badge the only channel.

notes.suggestedFix: Use { status: { notIn: TERMINAL_REQUEST_STATUSES } } so the closed set has one definition.

notes.claim: requirement 44 makes the sidebar badge issue an unfiltered GET .../requests from every page for every signed-in member, and for an admin or manager that call still runs the whole spec-10 vacation aggregation — where before this spec only opening the Requests page triggered it

witness.detail: requests-badge-context.tsx:46 sends the call with no query. For a caller holding view-requests, listRequests:245 always attaches the vacation section, which runs findMany over all VacationRequests of the org with no take and no status predicate when status defaults to 'all', a second findMany over all VacationReserveTransactions for those memberships, and an O(members x requests) balance loop at :167-198. No written rule covers the load characteristics of this endpoint and I have no measurement, so it is a note — but it is the change in this diff that no numbered requirement examines.

notes.suggestedFix: The badge needs only counts.waitingOnMe and vacation.pendingCount; a count-only path for a query-less call would avoid the aggregation. Decide it in the spec, not in the service.

notes.claim: no case at any level asserts that a message body is absent from the history, so requirement 21 — the one rule separating the two panels — has no negative witness

witness.detail: I read RequestHistory.tsx and confirmed the renderer is correct: `describe()` returns 'X replied' for message_posted and never touches a body, so requirement 21 is implemented. But TC-01-E2E-01 asserts only positive containment (thread contains the message at :244, history contains 'created the request' at :248), TC-01-E2E-07 likewise at :462-465, and TC-01-INT-11 asserts the event's actorKind and actorMembershipId and never that it carries no body. A history renderer that printed message bodies would pass the whole suite. Demoted from the shard's blocker because the implementation is right and sweep 8 blocks on a test that is weakened, missing by id, or asserts the opposite of the spec — none of which applies.

notes.claim: selecting the Vacation type filter renders the requests empty state above a populated vacation section
